red_state_bound.proof_strength_for_b: The unit's 'a uvicorn sentinel meant the red state never bound' is true only of the stubbed test. Proof of the refusal semantics is adequate (removing the guard makes ValueError disappear, cli.main return 0 and _resolve_serve return a generated token). Proof of exposure is not: the test cannot bind at all, so red(b) alone is a logic red, not an exposure red. I re-derived the exposure separately: with the refusal reverted, `resextract serve --host 192.168.2.187 --allow-remote --token auto` really bound 192.168.2.187:8944 (owner pid verified mine) and `_resolve_serve` returned a generated token without raising. In that combined red state anonymous GET /api/status answered 200 with the store payload (db_path, schema_version 4) and /api/dockets 200 - a live anonymous LAN leak. With guard (a) intact the same bind is gated (C1 in-process literal-'auto' app: anon 401 / 'auto' 200), so red(b) alone would bind a remote listener under a secret the operator did not choose, without an anonymous read leak.
